authoring.contract_packet:
# Sys1 repository requirement packet A

This packet supplies a historical public requirement and its API context. It
contains no evaluated source diff, outcomes, later repair, or proposed diagnosis.
Author one narrow advisory rule from this requirement, keeping it inactive.

## Requirement

Repository: https://github.com/hraness/sys1

Source: `AGENTS.md`, commit `6870f6acde623fd56446ba8fd9e4cdaf39fc4ee7`,
lines 41–43:

> A backend that returned any HTTP response is definitive; only transport
> failures (no response) may re-dispatch, at most once, and never for a
> `backend/model` pinned request. Surface retries via `x-sysone-attempts`.

The public function documentation in `src/backends.ts` at that same commit says:

> Forward one already-validated System One request body to a backend. Only
> transport failures (no HTTP response at all) report `transport`; any HTTP
> response — including backend errors — is definitive and passed through.

## API context

`src/backends.ts` exports this result union:

```ts
export type ForwardResult =
  | { kind: "response"; status: number; body: string; content_type: string }
  | { kind: "transport"; detail: string };
```

The forwarding function accepts a configured backend, a serialized validated
request, an optional resolved model ID, a timeout in milliseconds, and an
injectable Fetch implementation. It returns `Promise<ForwardResult>`.
`src/gateway.ts` owns the request routing and retry loop. The guidance applies
to both hosted and operator-configured backends.

Rule path: `src/backends.ts`. Use an `ensure` and a `breaks` statement derived
from the requirement. Do not add unsupported requirements or assume surrounding
code that a selected diff does not show.

# Blinded rule author note

Read exactly one domain-evidence file: `contract-only.md`.

Source packet SHA256: `981918b4a67d2341ad3075cdb6b2e5454e67f3d1de4bfcfa55c7fc5769a3c217`.

The packet's requirement and function documentation both distinguish receipt of an HTTP response from a transport failure with no response. The rule therefore covers only that distinction in `ForwardResult`. It does not impose gateway retry, pinning, or attempt-header requirements on `src/backends.ts`.

A selected hunk may omit the context needed to establish whether a response was received or which result is returned. Missing context alone does not establish the stated violation. The packet does not specify additional implementation mechanics, so none are required by this rule.

I read no evaluated defect, diff, repair, source snapshot, current implementation, history, manifest, result, sibling candidate file, or other conversation. I made no model, network, or test calls. This is inactive, source-only experimental material and will not be revised in response to predictions or results.

Clean labels concern only the selected response-finality requirement. Repair hunks 1 and 2 do not show the forwarding repair.
Rule wording and thresholds were frozen before predictions. The six recorded results are uncalibrated observations of this case, not a general accuracy estimate.
